triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: his master, who was also perhaps his father—Fyodor Pavlovitch

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: they would, in fact, have suspected the son of the murdered man, Dmitri Fyodorovitch.

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: deceived his master, whom he loved as his benefactor.

triples.subject: Grigory
triples.quote: on the night of the murder, there were five persons in Fyodor Pavlovitch’s—Fyodor Pavlovitch himself (but he did not kill himself, that’s evident); then his servant, Grigory

triples.subject: Marfa Ignatyevna
triples.quote: the third person was Grigory’s wife, Marfa Ignatyevna, but it would be simply shameful to imagine her murdering her master.

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: The first person who cried out that Smerdyakov had committed the murder was the prisoner himself at the moment of his arrest

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch Karamazov
triples.quote: If we are to believe the prisoner’s statement that he is not the murderer, then Smerdyakov must have been

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: So it may be supposed that the poor fellow suffered pangs of remorse at having deceived his master, whom he loved as his benefactor.
